metadata.title: How much time do adults spend on the PIAAC assessment and why does it matter?

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The analysis uses PIAAC computer-based assessment log files and restricts the sample to participants assigned to the literacy and numeracy modules. The note in the figure captions indicates that only those module-assigned participants are included, which implies a task/module-based analytic restriction rather than a full-sample use of all PIAAC respondents. The document does not report the use of complex survey weights or replicate weights for estimation of country differences in time-on-task and disengagement rates. Because the paper is descriptive and does not present PV-based achievement modeling, the weighting strategy (if any) is not specified; analysts should consult the PIAAC technical documentation for the appropriate sampling weights when producing population-representative estimates.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This OECD brief is primarily descriptive, focusing on log-file timing indicators (total time on task, item-level time percentiles, and T-disengagement rates) rather than modeling cognitive achievement scores that would require plausible values. As a result, plausible-value handling is not applicable to the reported outcomes. The document also does not describe any missing-data procedure for the log-derived indicators, which is a reporting gap for transparency, though it may be limited because the indicators are computed from recorded interaction events for module-assigned participants.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The sample includes only participants to the computer-based assessment who were assigned to the literacy and numeracy modules (as stated in the figure notes). The reported timing indicators are computed from PIAAC log files for those module-assigned participants; no additional inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., minimum log completeness thresholds) are specified in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD “Adult Skills in Focus” brief uses PIAAC computer-based assessment log files to study how much time adults spend on literacy and numeracy tasks, and how timing relates to item difficulty and disengagement. The analysis is restricted to participants assigned to the literacy and numeracy modules and computes descriptive indicators such as total time on task, within-item time percentiles, and T-disengagement rates (based on a minimum time threshold needed to attempt items). Large cross-country differences are reported: respondents in Austria, Finland, Germany, and Norway take about 50 minutes on average, while Ireland, Italy, Slovakia, Spain, and the UK take about 40 minutes. The brief also reports that time-on-task increases with age and education, is lower for respondents more familiar with ICT, and shows small gender differences. Finally, it estimates an average within-person causal effect of spending one additional second on an item on the probability of answering correctly (0.6 percentage points), while noting that PIAAC is low-stakes and disengagement can bias proficiency comparisons.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a descriptive OECD analysis of PIAAC log-file timing and disengagement indicators rather than an empirical machine-learning study with predictive modeling, so there are no ML algorithms, PV handling, or predictive performance metrics to extract. The absence of a reported analytic sample size and per-country Ns is consistent with the brief’s focus on illustrative cross-country comparisons using log-derived indicators, but it limits the ability to assess precision and representativeness.
